text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: I’ll pull the latest EXCAVA performance logs (excava_perf_2024-06-20.csv) and the vendor spec sheets (Caterpillar_994K_v3.2.pdf, Liebherr_R9800_v4.1.pdf) into /power/benchmarks/. Then I’ll run a 60-minute synthetic dig cycle on the 994K against the R9800 using the new 120-ton bucket (PN: 120T-HD-REV3) to capture raw cycle-time deltas. If the 994K edges ahead by ≥0.5 %, I’ll freeze the artifact as excava_994K_0.5pct_improvement.json and notify the lead; otherwise I’ll iterate with the R9800’s 130-ton bucket (PN: 130T-HD-REV2) next.

name: Torque
text: Torque: Gearbox, you’re benchmarking two excavators against each other—but where’s the *real* performance ceiling? The 994K and R9800 are already 4th-gen beasts; a 0.5% bump from a bucket swap is noise unless you prove the *dig cycle* itself is the bottleneck. Pull the torque curves from those PDFs and overlay them with the *actual* soil resistance data from excava_perf_2024-06-20.csv. If the synthetic cycle doesn’t stress the hydraulic limits, you’re optimizing for a phantom. Show me the delta in *energy per cubic meter*—not just cycle time.

name: Gearbox
text:
Gearbox (power-w1): I’ll extract the torque curves from Caterpillar_994K_v3.2.pdf and Liebherr_R9800_v4.1.pdf into /power/benchmarks/torque_curves.csv (columns: rpm, torque_Nm, model), then overlay them with the 120T-HD-REV bucket’s dig cycle data from excava_perf_2024-06-20.csv (rows: timestamp, rpm, torque_Nm, model). Using `pd.merge()` in Python, I’ll flag RPM bands where torque drops >5% below spec—those are the bottlenecks. Next, I’ll cross-reference with the 994K’s hydraulic pump PN: 105-6789-01 service bulletin to see if a 1500cc upgrade (PN: 105-6790-02) closes the gap.

name: Torque
text: Torque (power-checker): Gearbox, you’re still chasing *static* specs—torque curves don’t tell me if the 120T-HD-REV bucket’s geometry chokes the dig cycle at high RPM or if the 994K’s hydraulic relief valve is already maxed out. Pull the *hydraulic flow vs. pressure* data from those PDFs and overlay it with the bucket’s dig cycle *pressure spikes*—if the system’s hitting relief before peak torque, your 0.5% "bump" is a rounding error. And where’s the thermal throttling check? These beasts overheat in 30 minutes under load—prove the bucket swap doesn’t push them into derate territory.
